newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mills reject Canadian, U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila mills reject Canadian, U.S. wheat.

text.p: Four Manila flour millers rejected for the second time on Wednesday offers for the supply of 70,000 tonnes of Canadian and U.S. wheat saying the prices were too high, an executive at one of the mills said.
U.S. suppliers dropped their offer price to $193 per tonne from the $195 they had offered in the morning, the executive said.
Canadian suppliers quoted a price of $188 per tonne, down from $190 they quoted earlier.
"These prices are still too high for us. We expect prices to come down," he said.

Earlier on Wednesday after the firms rejected the first offer, another official told Reuters: We believed that prices are artificially being raised by speculators and it's not proper for wheat importers like the Philippines to be sucked up by this market."
The firms had sought the tenders late on Tuesday for April and May shipments.
